title: Route experiment v2: harder tasks, rubric-and-rank judges, gate probe

dispatch_flags.note: Every dispatch: headless, all tools allowed, no ask_user, no built-in MCP servers, no auto-update mid-run. Excluded tools keep each arm hermetic: no subagent or skill delegation (the arm's model mix is exactly what it claims), no cross-session history (this repo's own sessions wrote the oracles), no memory writes into the user's account, no web. Read-only stages additionally deny the write tool; judges also deny the shell.

role_profiles.note: task_profiles keys in data/pricing.copilot.json, used ONLY for the pre-dispatch ceiling estimate; measured AIC replaces the estimate once a dispatch finishes.

A2.label: Sol 6 plans -> Luna 6 (max) tests/builds/verifies -> Opus 5.5 reviews

A7.label: Sol 6 plans -> Luna 6 (max) tests/builds/verifies, no reviewer

rework.note: A verifier FAIL buys one implementer rework and one re-verify. A reviewer REJECT buys one implementer rework and one re-verify (no second review). In the reviewed shape (A6) a REJECT buys one solo rework and one re-review. Nothing else loops.

judging.note: v2 judges answer a per-task checklist rubric AND rank every candidate in one dispatch. A consistency_fraction share of (task, repeat) groups is judged a second time by every judge under a fresh shuffle; those re-judgments measure test-retest reliability and never enter the score.

probe.note: Spend-gated gate probe: each distinct pipeline verifier/reviewer stage sees each task's known-bad naive.patch and known-good reference.patch; sensitivity = rejects bad, specificity = accepts good.

scoring.note: Preregistered before any live v2 trial. Differences from v1: median-normalised simplicity, v2 mutation operators with a 50-mutant cap, rubric+rank judge quality, and a judge agreement gate (Kendall's W) below which judge quality leaves the score for every arm. Ties: gap <= equivalence_margin (3 QS, matched to the 18-pair design's ~2-3 point sensitivity) or a CI containing 0; among tied arms within cost_tie_pct % of the cheapest's mean AIC, the fastest median wall time wins. An arm with more than max_estimate_share of its AIC charged at estimate is flagged.
